notes: Cats: the Régionale bank splits the vine from the ground (Viticulture & Winemaking carries the cycle, pests, pruning and climate; Soil & Terroir the soils), the Village bank the same two ways (Viticulture & Winemaking; Terroir: Climate & Soil holds the climate scales, degree days, moderators and the named soils). Chapters: the one Régionale chapter and the two Village chapters that teach the Court's factors. Regions: every region the Court names on these pages, the eight whose soils both columns must be matched (Champagne, Chablis and the Côte d'Or inside burgundy, Haut-Médoc, Pomerol and St.-Émilion inside bordeaux, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Cornas, Hermitage and Côte-Rôtie inside rhone, Mosel) plus Coonawarra and Gimblett Gravels (hawkes-bay) from the Certified soil list and the moderator examples (Alsace, Napa and Sonoma, Columbia Valley, Mendoza); the Chile country record carries the Humboldt Current. No grapes: the Court names Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay, Riesling and Syrah only as examples of vinifera. Techniques: the vineyard and terroir groups of the roster, one door per Court factor (training, phylloxera, organic and biodynamic, frost, heat and irrigation, clones, canopy and yield, harvest, slopes for topography, altitude and diurnal range, sea and fog, soils). No service table applies.
